Prevention: Till, irrigate regularly; lay mulch on the ground to keep humid and warm, thus preventing frost; get rid of stagnant water during raining season.
Prune during the winter to remove the infected twigs and leaves as well as the overcrowded ones; rake the fallen leaves and bury them outside the garden so as to reduce overwintering pathogen source.
Careful pruning to avoid physical damages, reducing the infection.
Careful harvesting and post harvest treatment of fruit is needed to prevent post-harvest losses.
Monitoring: Intensive monitoring to be carried out from
September using 5 points sampling method at each plot; 100 to 200 leaves to be detected for the symptoms.
Symptoms: water-soaked, dark green lesions appear at leaf edge and leaf apex at earlier infection phase, then the lesions expand to cloud- like, yellow brown round lesions.

When climate is humid, dark red, sticky liquid drops could be found at the infected parts; when climate is dry, the infected parts turns to grey white and become dried, with large number of dark spots.
Direct control should be carried out immediately when leaves, twigs or fruits get infected.
Direct Control: Pruning infected leaves, twigs and fruits; burying them outside the garden.
Restrictions: Chemical pesticides must be applied strictly according to the prescribed dosages to avoid residue problems
Rotational application of pesticides to avoid resistance
PPEs is mandatory while using chemical pesticides
WHO U, Spray at the early phase of infection, PHI: 7 days
WHO II, Spray at the early phase of infection, PHI: 14 days
WHO II, Spray at the early phase of infection, PHI: 10~14 days
